let textPatchDescription: String = Self.textPatchDescription
        let shapePatchDescription: String = Self.shapePatchDescription
        var rows: [[String: Any]] = [

            // MARK: Clips

            opTool(
                "add_clip",
                "Places a whole media file as one clip at `at` on `track` — dragging a Media-tab "
                    + "row onto a track. The clip starts at source time 0 and runs the media's "
                    + "whole length snapped DOWN to whole frames, so it never outruns the file; "
                    + "trim it afterwards with trim_start / trim_end. It is given "
                    + "Fit scale when the project's fit_new_clips is on and the source is bigger "
                    + "than the canvas. Refused when it would break the overlap rule: a clip may "
                    + "overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap must be at "
                    + "most half of the shorter of the two clips (an overlap IS a transition).",
                [
                    "track": trackDescription,
                    "media": "Media id — import_media returns one.",
                    "at": "Start on the timeline, \(ticks)",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "add_text_clip",
                "Adds a text clip — a title. It has no source, so it can be any length; the "
                    + "default is 5 s of the Title preset, centred. Style it afterwards with "
                    + "set_text and place it with set_video (x, y, scale).",
                [
                    "track": trackDescription,
                    "at": "Start, \(ticks)",
                    "duration": "Length \(ticks) Default 5 s (3000000).",
                    // The op takes a set_text PATCH, which is what the core
                    // publishes; the STRING beside it is the app's shorthand
                    // and is a declared row rather than a type written here
                    // (`AgentCatalog+Declarations.swift`).
                    "text": "The words, or the styling too. A plain string is "
                        + "shorthand for {\"content\": …}; an object is a set_text patch "
                        + "merged over the Title preset. " + textPatchDescription
                        + " Default: the Title preset's placeholder.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "add_shape_clip",
                "Adds a shape clip — a rectangle, ellipse, line or arrow drawn over the video. "
                    + "Like text it has no source and any duration; set_shape changes its "
                    + "geometry and paint, set_video places it.",
                [
                    "track": trackDescription,
                    "at": "Start, \(ticks)",
                    "duration": "Length \(ticks) Default 5 s (3000000).",
                    // Optional, as the op is: omitted, the core's default
                    // rectangle lands. Declaring it a REQUIRED kind name put
                    // that default out of reach and made the box and the
                    // paint need a following set_shape.
                    "shape": "Which shape, and how it is drawn. A plain string is a "
                        + "kind — " + shapeNames.joined(separator: ", ")
                        + " — and an object is a set_shape patch merged over the default "
                        + "rectangle. " + shapePatchDescription + " Omit it for that "
                        + "rectangle; a rounded one is a rectangle with a radius, not a "
                        + "kind of its own. An arrow is created with its head on — pass "
                        + "arrow_end: false for a bare diagonal.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "add_adjustment_clip",
                "Adds an adjustment clip — Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip. It has no picture of its "
                    + "own: while it lasts it grades everything drawn BEHIND it (every lower "
                    + "track and the canvas background, never a track in front) with the "
                    + "colour and the point filters (sepia, noir, vignette, invert) that "
                    + "set_video gives it, and its opacity is the grade's strength. On a track "
                    + "cut by a matte it grades only inside the matte; on a matte track it does "
                    + "nothing. Refused inside a nest and in any transition or overlap — fade "
                    + "it with opacity instead; blur, sharpen, pixelate and a blend mode are "
                    + "errors on it.",
                [
                    "track": trackDescription,
                    "at": "Start, \(ticks)",
                    "duration": "Length \(ticks) Default 5 s (3000000).",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "add_background",
                "Puts a backdrop on a NEW back-most track, starting at 0 and running the "
                    + "timeline's length — Clip ▸ Add Background. With no arguments at all it "
                    + "is a canvas-sized WHITE rectangle, which is what the menu's Solid Color "
                    + "row sends: white rather than black because the canvas is already black, "
                    + "so a black plate would be a command that appears to do nothing. Give it "
                    + "a color to paint the plate another colour, or a media to put that "
                    + "picture there instead, at FILL scale — where add_clip would Fit it, "
                    + "because a plate that leaves the canvas showing down one side has "
                    + "failed at that. A video or audio plate stops where its file does, an "
                    + "image runs the timeline. A full-canvas GRADIENT is this clip and a "
                    + "set_shape {gradient} after it. media and color are alternatives: both "
                    + "is an error, as is a sub-frame duration or media, or one with no pictures.",
                [
                    "media": "Media id to show as the background — get_project lists "
                        + "them and import_media adds a file. Omit for a colour plate. A "
                        + "timed media is clamped to its own file's length, so a short movie "
                        + "stops where its file does; only an image runs the whole timeline.",
                    "color": colorDescription("The plate's colour; white when omitted"),
                    "duration": "Length \(ticks) Default: the whole timeline's length, "
                        + "and never less than one frame.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "add_blurred_background",
                "The screencast backdrop — Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background. `clip` is copied "
                    + "onto a NEW back-most track at the same start, duration, speed and "
                    + "source window, so the two play exactly the same frames, and the copy is "
                    + "scaled to FILL the canvas, centred, uncropped, blended normal and "
                    + "blurred at full strength. It is MUTED — its enabled becomes {video: "
                    + "true, audio: false}, or the mix would play one recording twice — and it "
                    + "drops the original's audio.duck along with its transition, actions and "
                    + "label. The duck goes because it is the one field of that group that "
                    + "lowers OTHER material: a copy keeping it would duck the whole mix, "
                    + "including the clip it was copied from. It is named \"Blurred "
                    + "Background\". Two objects are created, so new_tracks and new_clips both "
                    + "come back and the TRACK holds the lower id. An error for a NEST (the "
                    + "flattening drops a nest clip's own filters, so the copy would come out "
                    + "sharp), a source with no pixel size (a text clip, an audio-only one), "
                    + "or a clip carrying no video properties.",
                ["clip": clipDescription]),
            opTool(
                "insert_clip",
                "The INSERT edit — Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead, or ⌥-dropping a Media-tab row. "
                    + "Makes room for the whole media at `at`: the clip `at` is inside on "
                    + "`track` is split first, then every unlocked track opens by the media's "
                    + "length, then the media lands in the hole. Only the destination track is "
                    + "cut — a clip straddling `at` on another track rides the shift whole, "
                    + "which is what keeps a music bed unbroken — but for a cut clip's linked "
                    + "partner on an unlocked track, which is cut at `at` too and paired with "
                    + "it. One undo step.",
                [
                    "track": trackDescription,
                    "media": "Media id — import_media returns one.",
                    "at": "Where to insert, \(ticks)",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "overwrite_clip",
                "The OVERWRITE edit — Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead, or ⇧⌥-dropping a Media-tab "
                    + "row. Takes the room instead of making it: the span the media needs is "
                    + "cleared on `track` ALONE — cut at both bounds, whatever is left inside "
                    + "removed — and nothing shifts, so the cut's length and every other track "
                    + "are untouched, but for a cut clip's linked partner on an unlocked track, "
                    + "which is cut at the same bounds and paired; the partner's middle piece "
                    + "stays, unlinked. One undo step.",
                [
                    "track": trackDescription,
                    "media": "Media id — import_media returns one.",
                    "at": "Where to overwrite, \(ticks)",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "move_clip",
                "Shifts clips along the timeline by delta ticks (negative moves left; starts "
                    + "clamp at 0) and optionally onto another track — the timeline's clip drag. "
                    + "Several clips keep their relative track offsets. Refused when the "
                    + "destination would break the overlap rule (at most one neighbour "
                    + "overlapped on each side, each overlap at most half the shorter clip); a "
                    + "clip that gains an overlap with the clip before it also gains a "
                    + "cross_dissolve transition if it had none. A detach_audio pair moves "
                    + "together in time, but only the named clips change track.",
                [
                    "clips": clipsDescription,
                    "delta": "How far to shift, \(ticks) Negative moves earlier.",
                    "track": "Destination track id for the first clip; omit to stay "
                        + "on the current tracks.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "trim_start",
                "Moves a clip's START to `to`, keeping the content in place: the source "
                    + "in-point advances by the same amount, so nothing after the new start "
                    + "shifts. Clamped by the source's own beginning and by the clip's end (a "
                    + "clip is at least one frame long). On a clip with a speed ramp the ramp "
                    + "stays where it is in the clip, so what plays after the new start can "
                    + "change, and the start is held where the clip still fits its media. On a "
                    + "detach_audio pair the other half's start follows when it was the same.",
                ["clip": clipDescription, "to": "New start, \(ticks)", "alone": aloneDescription]),
            opTool(
                "trim_end",
                "Moves a clip's END to `to`. Clamped by how much source is left after the "
                    + "in-point, on the frame grid, and by the clip's start. On a detach_audio "
                    + "pair the other half's end follows when it was the same.",
                ["clip": clipDescription, "to": "New end, \(ticks)", "alone": aloneDescription]),
            opTool(
                "rate_stretch",
                "Stretches a clip to end at `to_end` by changing its SPEED instead of trimming "
                    + "it — the whole source still plays, faster or slower (⌥-dragging the end "
                    + "edge). Media clips only: a text, shape, image or freeze clip has no "
                    + "source to stretch and is an error. A speed ramp on the clip scales with "
                    + "it; a stretch that would take any of its rates past the limits changes "
                    + "nothing. "
                    + "Captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are "
                    + "re-timed with it in the same step: captions_retimed lists them, and "
                    + "captions_removed those whose speech it no longer plays.",
                ["clip": clipDescription, "to_end": "New end, \(ticks)"]),
            opTool(
                "slip",
                "Slides the SOURCE under a fixed clip — ⌥⇧-dragging a clip's body. What the "
                    + "clip shows changes; where it sits does not, so nothing downstream moves. "
                    + "`delta` is timeline ticks and the source moves by delta × the clip's "
                    + "speed; a positive delta shows LATER material. Clamped so the window "
                    + "stays inside the media, and a slip the clamps reduce to nothing changes "
                    + "nothing. A freeze clip moves the frame it holds instead. Media and "
                    + "freeze clips only: any other kind is an error.",
                [
                    "clip": clipDescription,
                    "delta": "How far to slide the source, \(ticks)",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "roll",
                "Moves a hard CUT — ⌥⇧-dragging a clip's edge. This clip's start and its "
                    + "predecessor's end both become `to`: one clip grows by exactly what the "
                    + "other loses, and the pair's outer edges and total length do not move. "
                    + "The predecessor is the clip on the same track ending EXACTLY at this "
                    + "one's start; with a gap or an overlap there instead, it is refused (an "
                    + "overlap is a transition — use set_transition_duration). Clamped so each "
                    + "clip keeps a frame and neither asks for source it does not have. The "
                    + "linked half of a detach_audio pair rolls its own cut too when it starts "
                    + "at the same time.",
                [
                    "clip": clipDescription, "to": "Where the cut moves to, \(ticks)",
                    "alone": aloneDescription,
                ]),
            opTool(
                "split",
                "Cuts clips in two at `at` — Clip ▸ Split (⌘T). The second piece keeps playing the source from "
                    + "where the first stopped, and each keeps the animation actions that fall "
                    + "on its side (an action straddling the cut becomes two). With no clips "
                    + "every unlocked clip under the time is split, which is what the menu "
                    + "command does with nothing selected. Refused when `at` is not strictly "
                    + "inside a clip.",
                [
                    "clips": "Clip ids; omit to split every unlocked clip at `at`.",
                    "at": "Where to cut, \(ticks) Default: the playhead.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "delete",
                "Removes clips and LEAVES the gaps where they were — ⌫. Use ripple_delete to "
                    + "close them. Deleting a detach_audio picture deletes its sound too; "
                    + "deleting the sound alone keeps the picture, silent.",
                ["clips": clipsDescription]),
            opTool(
                "ripple_delete",
                "Removes clips and closes the gaps: everything starting after each removed span "
                    + "on an UNLOCKED track slides left by that span's length — ⌘⌫. Clips on "
                    + "locked tracks and clips that straddle a span stay where they are.",
                ["clips": clipsDescription]),
            opTool(
                "ripple_delete_range",
                "Cuts a time range out of the whole timeline: every unlocked clip is split at "
                    + "both bounds, the middles are removed, and the rest slides left by the "

+ "both bounds, the middles are removed, and the rest slides left by the "
                    + "range's length. The in/out-range form of ⌘⌫.",
                ["from": "Range start, \(ticks)", "to": "Range end, \(ticks)"]),
            opTool(
                "ripple_delete_ranges",
                "Cuts SEVERAL time ranges out of the whole timeline as ONE edit — what Clip ▸ "
                    + "Remove Silences… sends. Each pair is put in order (a reversed pair is "
                    + "the same range), the pairs are then MERGED — overlapping and touching "
                    + "alike — and the survivors are cut right to left exactly as "
                    + "ripple_delete_range cuts one. So this is NOT the same as calling that "
                    + "once per pair: two ranges that meet make one shift, not two. It is one "
                    + "undo step however many ranges there are, which is the point. Markers do "
                    + "not move, as under every ripple. An empty list, and a list that merges "
                    + "to nothing, change nothing. detect_silence returns ranges in this shape.",
                ["ranges": "The spans to cut, each a [from, to] pair \(ticks)"]),
        ]
        // detect_silence and normalize_clip are `AgentCatalog+Audio.swift`'s,
        // spliced in HERE rather than appended, so the catalog's order is
        // unchanged — road map 4's toll 2. `ticks` and `clipsProperty` are
        // the two hoisted locals they read.
        rows += audioTools(ticks: ticks, clipsProperty: clipsProperty)
        rows += [
            opTool(
                "lift_range",
                "Cuts a time range out and LEAVES the hole — ⌫ with an in/out range and nothing "
                    + "selected. Every unlocked clip is split at both bounds and the middles "
                    + "removed, and nothing moves: every clip after the range keeps the moment "
                    + "it had, which is what makes this the safe cut when a mix or a caption "
                    + "track is already timed. Use ripple_delete_range to close the hole "
                    + "instead.",
                ["from": "Range start, \(ticks)", "to": "Range end, \(ticks)"]),
            opTool(
                "insert_time",
                "Opens a gap: every unlocked clip starting at or after `at` moves right by "
                    + "`length`. Straddling clips are left in place, so this makes room without "
                    + "cutting anything — split first if you want the gap inside a clip. Every "
                    + "marker at or after `at` moves right by `length` too.",
                [
                    "at": "Where the gap opens, \(ticks)",
                    "length": "How much room, \(ticks)",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "close_gap",
                "Closes the empty span on `track` that contains `at` — double-clicking a gap in "
                    + "a lane, or Clip ▸ Close Gap. The gap is bounded by the nearest clip "
                    + "edges on that track, and everything from its far side slides left by its "
                    + "length across every unlocked track. Nothing changes when `at` is on a "
                    + "clip, when the track is locked, when there is no clip after the gap, or "
                    + "when the shift would break the overlap rule — a gap closes fully or not "
                    + "at all.",
                [
                    "track": trackDescription,
                    "at": "A time inside the gap, \(ticks)",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "set_speed",
                String(
                    format: "Changes a clip's playback rate — Clip ▸ Speed… — or fits it to a "
                        + "duration — the Speed section's Fit to: give rate or duration, exactly "
                        + "one. Any non-media clip is an error. The duration follows (source "
                        + "length ÷ rate, snapped and held to what the file holds); actions keep "
                        + "their place. Rate is clamped to %g–%g. Above ×%g, with or without "
                        + "keep_pitch, the clip's audio is left out of the mix. On a clip with "
                        + "a speed ramp every rate in the ramp scales with it, so the ramp keeps "
                        + "its shape; the scale stops where any of its rates would pass the "
                        + "limits. Captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound "
                        + "are re-timed with it in the same step: captions_retimed lists them, "
                        + "and captions_removed those whose speech it no longer plays.",
                    speed.min,
                    speed.max, speed.audioMax),
                [
                    "clip": clipDescription,
                    "rate": "1 = normal, 2 = twice as fast (half as long), 0.5 = slow motion.",
                    "duration": "The length to fit the clip to, instead of a rate \(ticks)",
                    "keep_pitch": "Keep the audio's pitch at the new speed (default: as it is).",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "set_reversed",
                "Plays a media clip back to front, or forward again — the Reverse checkbox in the "
                    + "Clip tab's Timing section. Nothing "
                    + "about the timeline moves: the clip keeps its start, its duration and its "
                    + "in point, and the in point is measured in the direction the clip plays, "
                    + "so reversing a trimmed clip shows the other end of the file. Media clips "
                    + "only: any other kind is an error. The reversed frames are pre-rendered on "
                    + "the app side the first time they are needed, so the first render_frame or "
                    + "export after this may take a moment.",
                [
                    "clip": clipDescription,
                    "reversed": "true plays it backwards, false forwards again.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "freeze_frame",
                "Holds one frame: the clip is split at `at`, a gap of `duration` is opened, and "
                    + "a still of that exact source frame fills it with the clip's own video "
                    + "properties — ⇧⌘F. Media clips only.",
                [
                    "clip": clipDescription,
                    "at": "The moment to freeze, \(ticks) Default: the playhead.",
                    "duration": "How long to hold \(ticks) Default 2 s (1200000).",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "detach_audio",
                "Splits a clip's audio onto its own clip on the track below (inserting one when "
                    + "there is none), muting the original's audio and hiding the new clip's "
                    + "video — ⌥⌘D. The two are LINKED (`linked` names the other): moves, "
                    + "splits, ripples, nests and copies keep them in step in time; trim_start "
                    + "or trim_end with alone: true on the sound makes a J- or L-cut; speed and "
                    + "reverse are refused until attach_audio. Refused, saying why, for a "
                    + "non-media clip, media with no audio, or audio already detached.",
                ["clip": clipDescription]),
            opTool(
                "attach_audio",
                "Merges a detach_audio pair back into one clip — Clip ▸ Attach Audio "
                    + "(⇧⌥⌘D). Name either half. The picture's audio comes back on with the "
                    + "sound's audio settings and the sound clip goes. Refused when the clip is "
                    + "not linked, and when the two no longer cover the same time (a J- or "
                    + "L-cut): trim them to match first.",
                ["clip": clipDescription]),
            opTool(
                "duplicate",
                "Copies clips onto the same tracks, placed immediately after the originals' "
                    + "span — ⌘D. Follow with move_clip to put them anywhere else.",
                ["clips": clipsDescription]),
            opTool(
                "paste",
                "Inserts a clipboard payload's clips with fresh ids — ⌘V. The earliest clip in "
                    + "the payload lands exactly at `at` and the others keep their offsets from "
                    + "it, so a copied arrangement pastes back intact. The payload is what Copy "
                    + "(⌘C) put on the pasteboard: {\"clips\": [...], \"media\": [...]}, whose "
                    + "clips are get_project's clip objects and whose media are its media rows. "
                    + "TWO things differ from get_project's spelling. A payload clip's `track` "
                    + "is a DEPTH from the front of the track stack (0 = front-most, 1 the lane "
                    + "behind it), not a track id, because the ids belong to the project it was "
                    + "copied from; and media is matched to this project's media[] BY PATH, so a "
                    + "row it does not have is added and one it does is reused. Ids in the "
                    + "payload are ignored — everything is re-minted. A clip the overlap rule "
                    + "refuses on its target track is placed on a new track in front rather "
                    + "than dropped.",
                [
                    "at": "Where the earliest clip lands, \(ticks) Default: the "
                        + "playhead.",
                    "track": "Track id for the payload's depth 0; the rest follow by "
                        + "the same offset. Default: the front-most track.",
                    "payload": "{\"clips\": [...], \"media\": [...]} — see above.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "paste_attributes",
                "Copies the payload's EARLIEST clip's property groups onto each of the clips — "
                    + "Edit ▸ Paste Attributes (⌥⌘V). The payload is the same Copy payload paste "
                    + "takes; only its earliest clip is read (at one start the front-most, then "
                    + "the lower id — never the array's first, which is creation order), and its "
                    + "ids and media rows do not matter. Each group REPLACES the target's whole "
                    + "group — video and audio whole (position and scale included), text but its "
                    + "content, a shape but its kind, width, height, from and to. Left out, "
                    + "`groups` means each of video, audio, text and shape BOTH clips have, "
                    + "silently skipping the rest; a named group the payload clip lacks, or a "
                    + "target lacks, is an error, and so is a value the inspector would refuse. "
                    + "`graphic` travels only when NAMED (Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties): the "
                    + "props, whole, onto clips drawn by the SAME graphic, each keeping its name, "
                    + "size, in and length, and any prop the payload lacks that an action on that "
                    + "clip animates, which stays so the ramp keeps its start; a clip of another "
                    + "graphic is an error naming both. The props are checked for shape only, when "
                    + "a target takes them. Speed, enabled, actions, the transition and the clip's "
                    + "own name and label stay. A video qualifier follows the clip kind: dropped "
                    + "onto a picture clip, an adjustment clip's own kept when the payload clip is "
                    + "not an adjustment clip, copied between two. Refused (no change) when "
                    + "nothing changes.",
                [
                    "clips": clipsDescription,
                    "payload": "What Copy wrote, {\"clips\": [...], \"media\": [...]}; see paste.",
                    // The names are the CORE's (`Kind::Groups`); a refusal names the handler's.
                    "groups": "Which groups travel. Default: each of video, audio, text and "
                        + "shape both clips have, never graphic; an empty list is refused.",
                    "skip_missing": "true: with groups named, a group the payload clip lacks is "
                        + "dropped and a clip that cannot take one is skipped. Default false.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "nest",
                "Collapses clips into ONE clip that stands for the group — ⌘G. The clips move "
                    + "whole (properties, actions, transitions) onto the nest's own tracks, "
                    + "keeping their relative times and their stacking order with the earliest "
                    + "starting at 0; the nest clip lands on the front-most track the selection "
                    + "occupied and runs from the earliest start to the latest end. From then on "
                    + "the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing, and the "
                    + "nest's canvas is frozen at the project's current size so a later "
                    + "set_canvas cannot re-lay-out what is inside. get_project lists the groups "
                    + "under `nests`, each with its own tracks and clips. Refused (no change) on "
                    + "an empty selection, on a single clip that is already a nest, and when the "
                    + "nest clip would overlap something that was not selected.",
                [
                    "clips": clipsDescription,
                    "name": "What to call the group. Default: Nest <n>.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "unnest",
                "Opens a nest clip: its contents return to the timeline and the nest clip goes — "
                    + "⇧⌘G. The exact inverse of nest apart from the ids, which are minted "
                    + "fresh. Clips land at the nest clip's start plus their own, on tracks "
                    + "counted back from the nest clip's own (tracks missing behind it are "
                    + "added), and one the overlap rule refuses goes on a new track in front "
                    + "rather than being dropped. A nest clip trimmed shorter than its contents "
                    + "gives ALL of them back — trimming a nest hides content rather than "
                    + "cutting it. An error on any clip that is not a nest.",
                ["clip": clipDescription]),
        ]
        // set_video, set_audio, set_text, set_shape and set_clip are
        // `AgentCatalog+Properties.swift`'s, spliced in HERE, after `unnest`,
        // so the catalog's order is unchanged.
        rows += propertyTools(clipsDescription: clipsDescription)
        rows += [
            opTool(
                "set_enabled",
                "Turns one clip's video and/or audio on or off — the two halves detach_audio "
                    + "flips. A disabled half contributes nothing to the composition but the "
                    + "clip stays where it is.",
                [
                    "clip": clipDescription,
                    "video": "Show this clip's picture.",
                    "audio": "Play this clip's sound.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "set_transition",
                "Sets the transition INTO a clip — the one that plays across its overlap with "
                    + "the clip before it on the same track. The transition's duration IS that "
                    + "overlap, so a clip with no overlap ignores it: make one with move_clip or "
                    + "set_transition_duration. kind null removes it.",
                [
                    "clip": clipDescription,
                    // The null beside the core's thirteen names, and the
                    // required-ness that keeps a forgotten kind from becoming
                    // one, are both declared rows
                    // (`AgentCatalog+Declarations.swift`).
                    "kind": "The transition, or null to remove it.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "set_transition_duration",
                "Makes a clip's transition last `duration` by MOVING the clip so its overlap "
                    + "with the clip before it equals that. Refused on a track's first clip and past "
                    + "half the shorter clip (snapped down), naming that limit.",
                ["clip": clipDescription, "duration": "Overlap length, \(ticks)"]),
        ]
        rows += actionTools(ticks: ticks, clipDescription: clipDescription)
        return rows
    }
}

import Foundation

// MARK: - Catalog: clip properties

/// The catalog's five PROPERTY rows — `set_video`, `set_audio`, `set_text`,
/// `set_shape` and `set_clip`, the patches that change a clip's base
/// property groups — and the patch vocabulary they are written in.
///
/// A pure move out of `AgentCatalog+Clips.swift` (grading GR1), which stood
/// over app/CLAUDE.md's ~600-line cap with grading's own patch prose still to
/// land. The five rows came here whole, in their existing order, with their
/// bodies untouched, and are SPLICED back in where they left — after
/// `unnest`, before `set_enabled` — by `clipAndActionTools`, so the catalog's
/// order is unchanged. The hoisted locals they read came with them as
/// `static let`s, each with its own name, comment and an explicit type, so
/// every one stays its own expression for the type checker's budget. Three are internal rather than private — `shapeNames`,
/// `textPatchDescription` and `shapePatchDescription` — because
/// `add_text_clip` and `add_shape_clip`, which stayed, read them through
/// typed locals of the same names. `clipsDescription` is the clips' sentence
/// and arrives as an argument rather than a second spelling here. The video
/// patch's vocabulary is `AgentCatalog+VideoPatch.swift`'s (road map
/// creator-jobs CU3a1's toll).
extension AgentServer {

    static let shapeNames: [String] = ShapeKind.allCases.map { $0.rawValue }
    private static let audioPatchDescription: String =
        "Audio properties to merge. Keys: volume (0–"

        + "fade_out (ticks), fade_in_shape and fade_out_shape (linear — the default — "
        + "s_curve, plus_3db for a fast start, minus_3db for a slow one), duck (null or "
        + "{level, attack, release, mode, pre_roll, hold}: mode extent — the default, for "
        + "the clip's whole length — or speech, only while the clip's speech plays, "
        + "widened by pre_roll before and hold after, in ticks, 0.5 s each by default; "
        + "speech saves the media's speech spans from its detected speech in the same "
        + "step, and is an error for a clip that is not a media clip with sound or whose "
        + "speech has not been detected yet), mono, keep_pitch, "
        + "pan (-1 hard left … +1 hard right), compressor (null or {threshold_db, ratio, "
        + "attack, release, makeup_db} — the two times in ticks), noise_reduction (0–1), "
        + "limiter (null or {ceiling_db, release}: a true-peak limiter last in the clip's "
        + "chain, ceiling_db in dBTP after the clip's base volume, -24 to 0, default -1, "
        + "release in ticks, 600 to 600000, default 60000; {limiter: {}} turns it on at "

    // Format 32's keys (spec §11 AU-31..AU-34), their own typed local so the
    // chain above stays short enough to type-check quickly. The presets' values

    private static let audioEQClause: String =

    private static let audioDynamicsClause: String =

        let textPatchDescription: String = Self.textPatchDescription
        let shapePatchDescription: String = Self.shapePatchDescription

                    + "behind_subject (Text Behind Subject) by any drawing clip but an "

                "set_audio",

/// tool cannot be declared without one.
extension AgentServer {

Default size is the module's meta size, else the canvas.","Width and height are bounded by the graphic side limits; a canvas side over 8192 is an error naming the canvas when no size is given.","At most 64 props.   mcp=["add_graphic_clip","insert_graphic"])
O("add_adjustment_clip","Add an adjustment clip","color","Adds a clip with no picture that grades everything drawn behind it while it lasts.",
  ["Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip"],
  ["5 s long by default.","Its colour, wheels, curves, look, point filters (sepia, noir, vignette, invert) and opacity (the grade's strength) reach every lower track and the canvas background, never a track in front.","On a track cut by a matte it grades only inside the matte; on a matte track it does nothing.","Refused inside a nest and in any transition or overlap; fade it with opacity instead.","Blur, sharpen, pixelate and blend modes are errors on it, and it cannot be nested."])
O("add_background","Add a background plate","canvas","Puts a colour plate or a picture behind everything on a new back-most track named Background.",

O("add_blurred_background","Add a blurred background","canvas","Puts a muted, blurred, full-canvas copy of a clip behind it on a new back-most track: the screencast backdrop.",
  ["Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background"],
  ["The copy has the same start, duration, speed and source window, so both play the same frames.","It is scaled to fill, centred, uncropped, blend normal, blurred at full strength, and named Blurred Background.","It is muted and drops its ducking, transition, actions and label.","Errors for a nest, a source with no pixel size (text, audio-only) or a clip with no video properties."])

  ["Only the destination track is cut, at both bounds, and the middle removed. Nothing shifts.","A cut clip's linked partner is cut at the same bounds; its middle piece stays, unlinked.","One undo step. A LUT media is refused."])

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with

  `onQueue` (main only, never on the store's queue) so no pass runs between
  their steps: `removeModule(named:)` keeps the file's bytes and then removes
  it, refusing when the text could not be kept, and `moveModule(from:to:)`
  moves the file, journals the pair and reads it back — a rename that cannot
  be journalled is refused — and then moves its history, a throw leaving the
  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`
  in `GraphicStore+History.swift`), so a refused rename journals no pair; a
  crash between the three steps is G-28 (f)'s limit; neither rescans.
  `write(name:bytes:)` is `write(name:source:)` for bytes as they are, and
  `noModuleSentence(_:)` the one sentence for an absent module.

  (spec §11 G-27..G-29): `graphics/history/<name>/<%06d sequence>-<revision>.js`,
  the last `historyLimit` (10) per module, and `history/renames.json`, at
  most `renameJournalLimit` (32) pairs. `keepReplaced`, called by `pass` on
  the queue before it stores its scan, keeps the bytes a module's new text
  replaced and drops the new text's own revision, so history never holds the
  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not
  make, and `start()` drops each module's current revision from its history.
  `history/` is created only inside an existing `graphics/` (G-14) with no
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` call, and `moveHistory` leaves no
  `history/<from>/` behind — which is what makes 'no file, something kept'

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,

  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,

  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and

  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`

  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil

  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.

  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what

  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`

  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.

  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);

  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written
  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor
  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,
  `hideIdleSteps` and `polished`,
  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is

  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an

  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is

  (GR-13), so a row writes

  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,

  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and

  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.

  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`

  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.

- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what

- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:

  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the

  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.

  where it is (`<package>/graphics`, or an untitled document's

  `packageDidMove(to:)` from the `fileURL` setter, posting
  `.graphicsLocationDidChange`), the scan (each legal `*.js` with its

  cannot use, warned and skipped, G-23 (e)) and the watch. **`graphics/` is created on the app's first write, never at
  open** (G-14): `ensureFolder()` is the ONE creator inside a package, and
  every app-side writer goes through `write(name:source:)` or it. While the
  folder is absent the store watches the PACKAGE directory, and the first
  observed appearance calls `folderDidAppear` →
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` once — without it the next save is
  refused as "changed by another application". A folder source raises
  `.write` only and an in-place save raises nothing on it (G0 q7), so each
  module, font and asset file has its own source, up to `fileSourceLimit` (16
  a pass, modules first, then fonts, then assets, each in name order; spec §11
  G-19 (c), G-20 (a)); a source whose `open` fails is a scan warning,
  "`<subject>` is not watched: open failed (`<strerror>`)", `errno` copied
  first (G-20 (b); `GraphicScan.warnings`, shown by the Source section and `get_graphic {}`,
  G-24 (b));
  every pass re-opens every source BY PATH and
  arms BEFORE it scans; events coalesce over 100 ms. The queue owns the diff
  and an outbox; main publishes in order through `drain()` (`scan`, the
  callback, `.graphicsDidChange` with sorted names — every module and
  `library: true` when the font/asset set moved; with NO names when the
  folder holds no module and only the library moved, which still posts, G5b).
  `GraphicStore+Files.swift` holds the store's own writes:
  `uniqueModuleName(_:)`, the one free-name rule (`-copy`, `-copy-N`)
  Duplicate and Insert ▸ Graphic share, which takes a name as held when the
  scan OR the disk has it (`holdsModule(named:)`, #75); `write(name:source:)`
  and `importFile` land through `land(at:writing:)`, whose `.partial` is
  removed on any failure; and `removeScratchRoot()`, which removes an untitled
  root after `stop()` — from `packageDidMove(to:)` and `stopGraphicStore()`
  (G-19 (d)). It also holds the app's delete and rename, each inside
  `onQueue` (main only, never on the store's queue) so no pass runs between
  their steps: `removeModule(named:)` keeps the file's bytes and then removes
  it, refusing when the text could not be kept, and `moveModule(from:to:)`
  moves the file, journals the pair and reads it back — a rename that cannot
  be journalled is refused — and then moves its history, a throw leaving the
  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`
  in `GraphicStore+History.swift`), so a refused rename journals no pair; a
  crash between the three steps is G-28 (f)'s limit; neither rescans.

  `noModuleSentence(_:)` the one sentence for an absent module.

  replaced and drops the new text's own revision, so history never holds the
  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.
